spans.text: When
allies are on opposite sides or corners of an opponent, so long as they are not under an effect that would prevent them from making
an Attack and they each also have an equipped
Weapon, they are both considered to be Flanking that opponent. Figures making a
Attack against a target they are Flanking Gain
TO THE ATK ROLL
Some Abilities give Adventurers and Combatants bonuses only when they are Flanking a target. For example, figures with the
BACKSTAB
Tag
Gain
+3 PHYSICAL DMG
when making a
Attack against a target they are Flanking.
Weapons with the
Icon cannot Gain the Flanking bonus. Figures with equipped
Weapons cannot grant another figure the Flanking
bonus.
Weapons with the Reach Tag may also Flank and provide opportunities for allies to Backstab. So long as a figure with Reach is attacking an
opponent while there is also another ally who is within Melee Range (or the Range of their own Reach Tag) of your target
and
on the opposite
side or corner of that same target, you Gain the Flanking bonus.
Below are some Diagrams to help explain this better:
Example 1:
In this example, Zeke and Rook are on the opposite side of the Shadow Lord as Remi, meaning they are both Flanking. Alternatively, it
means that Remi is also Flanking the Shadow Lord. The bonus granted by Flanking does not stack, Meaning, Rook and Remi and Zeke will all only Gain
to any Attacks they make against the Shadow Lord. Meanwhile, Remi is on the opposite side of the Animate as Nightingale, meaning in addition to
the Shadow Lord, Remi is also Flanking the Animate. However, Nightingale will only Gain an Attack bonus against the Animate.
Example 2:
When drawing Line of Sight via Reach, Combatants grant and can benefit from Flanking opponents. In this example, Remi has Reach
2. Rook does not. Even so, they are both considered Flanking since both figures are within Range to make a Melee Attack and on opposite sides of the
target.
Example 3:
If both Rook and Remi had Reach 2, they could both get the Flanking bonus against the Animate so long as both figures were in Melee
range and on opposite sides of the target.
Example 4:
In this example, let's assume that Rook and Remi each have Reach 2 Weapons equipped. Even though Rook and Remi could still make
an Attack against the Animate at Reach 2, neither are attacking from opposite ends of the target. Furthermore, since there is not a figure on opposite
sides of the target, they are also not granting Flanking to any allies. Another way to visualize this is to draw an imaginary line between the center of
each figure trying to determine if they are Flanking. If the line is drawn through
opposite corners
or
sides
of spaces the target occupies, then you are
Flanking. The blue line here represents what that might look like. You can see that it does not draw through opposite sides of the target. Meanwhile, both
Nightingale and Zeke could also Attack, but they would also not be considered Flanking for the same reasons.
Example 5:
Remember, when determining if you can flank from a corner, another ally must be able to attack the same target from the opposite corner.
In this case, both Zeke and Nightingale could flank but neither Remi or Rook could.
Example 6:
You can even use Reach 2 to Flank targets diagonally. This gives Remi and Rook a ton of range!
Example 7:
Line of Sight is still taken into account when using Reach Weapons. This means that friendly figures will still impart a -1 to Rook's ATK
Roll. However, since Rook is still within Melee Range of the target, he and Remi will still get a Flanking bonus.
Example 8:
If your Line of Sight is blocked to an opponent a figure may not Gain or contribute to Flanking that opponent. This means that in this
example, neither Rook or Remi would be able to Flank either target.
Example 9:
Flanking only requires that another ally on the opposite side of the target is also within Range to make a Melee Attack. This works the
same with Large Based Combatants. Reach simply expands your Melee Range. This means that the larger the base of the target you’re trying to flank, the
more spots there are to flank from!
Example 10:
You can see that being on opposite sides of a target and within Melee Range is all it takes to flank! The blue line is again drawn here to
show that both Remi and Rook are attacking from opposite sides. In the case of the larger figure, this has given them more room to work with as each
side is bigger making our imaginary line easier to draw between figures while also crossing opposite sides of the target.
